decisions.quote: We replicate Ferris and Graddy's classic 1986 study of local government production and sector choice to assess how public procurement has changed over the past 35 years. Our findings show that today, contracting out is more commonly used across 25 local government service areas. In contrast to the original study, much of the growth has been in government‐to‐government contracts. For profit firms are also winning more contracts for high transaction cost work, while nonprofits are receiving fewer government contracts in nearly every service area.
decisions.reason: Under Codebook Step 3 (Rule 2), coding a replication outcome without an overall verdict requires identifying the original study's specific empirical finding or prediction and the corresponding replication result that tests it. Here, the abstract states the aim is 'to assess how public procurement has changed over the past 35 years' and reports descriptive temporal shifts in contracting prevalence and sector composition ('more commonly used', 'much of the growth has been in government-to-government contracts', 'winning more contracts for high transaction cost work', and 'receiving fewer government contracts'). Even where it notes '[i]n contrast to the original study, much of the growth has been in government-to-government contracts,' it describes post-1986 growth and shifting sector shares over time without stating Ferris and Graddy's (1986) original empirical claims or theoretical predictions about local government production and sector choice or whether those relationships held. Because the original empirical findings and predictions are unspecified in the supplied text (and 'descriptive only' does not apply because the authors do not frame the study as merely applying the original methods in a new context without comparison), the outcome is undeterminable on this substantive basis.

scope_review.parent_objection: First reply returns undeterminable because abstract cannot rule out confirming comparisons in unseen full text. Codebook Rule2 asks us to code available original-specific comparisons, and not withhold one evidence states. Abstract explicitly says In contrast to the original study, much of the growth has been in government-to-government contracts; also states more for-profit high-transaction-cost contracts and fewer nonprofits. Is an actual original finding established and contrasted sufficiently to code failed from observed original comparisons, or is this merely descriptive time-change with original prediction unspecified (descriptive only/undeterminable)? Do not infer mixed merely because unseen full text might agree elsewhere. Identify original empirical finding and corresponding result required by Rule2; retain uncertainty if missing on that substantive basis.
